items.title: Perez gets a five-place Qatar drop after the Vegas clash
items.summary: Stewards' Document 61 found Perez wholly responsible for the Turn 14 collision with Rafael Câmara and converted his unserved 10-second penalty into five places at his next race. In a later Formula1.com report, Perez said he thought he was alongside; Câmara said he still needed to review what happened.
items.why_it_matters: Apply the five places in Qatar grid preparation. Keep the drivers' accounts separate from the stewards' finding and do not copy Vegas power-unit penalties or energy limits into Qatar event data.

items.title: Qatar's 27-lap cap, high pressures and conflicting set totals
items.summary: Two Formula1.com articles published on 25 November give different per-driver allocations: the 10:05 UTC guide says 2 C1 Hard, 3 C2 Medium and 8 C3 Soft, with an extra Soft reserved for Q3; the 10:43 UTC explainer says each driver gets 13 sets (2 C1, 4 C2, 7 C3). Pirelli's 24 November release confirms the compounds and 27-lap cap, but not set totals. The FIA competition visa confirms 57 race laps over 5.419 km and a 19:00 local start. Its separate Pirelli competition notes prescribe C1 and C2 as mandatory race tyres, C3 for Q3, and 27 laps per set across tyre history; they do not state the conflicting per-driver allocation. The Race's 26 November report says the FIA notes set minimum starting pressures at 29 psi front and 27.5 psi rear, the season's highest front minimum. It attributes front-left overheating, wear and soft graining concerns to Williams, and the risk of an early stop forcing a third stop to McLaren. These are team assessments, not a predicted or published race strategy. Pirelli's reported counting rules include Safety Car and Virtual Safety Car laps; all race laps from start signal to chequered flag count, an unfinished lap in other sessions counts in full, mixed-mileage sets take the higher count, and reconnaissance, formation and post-race laps are excluded.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the conflicting official F1 per-driver allocations explicitly attributed until clarified. The 29/27.5 psi figures are minimum starting pressures; the FIA table separately gives stabilized thresholds of 30/28.5 psi. Attribute the front-left and stop-timing assessments to the named teams, not as measured outcomes or official predicted strategy. Exact remaining-set counts still require a post-qualifying chart.

items.title: Tsunoda appeal still has no public ruling as Red Bull and McLaren fight for P3
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli clinched his first Drivers' Championship with third place in Mexico City on 1 November; Mercedes secured the Constructors' Championship in São Paulo on 8 November. After Las Vegas, Formula1.com lists Antonelli on 402 points to Max Verstappen's 304 and Mercedes on 666 to Ferrari's 517; Red Bull has 440 and McLaren 431, nine points apart for P3. Norris discussed the close contest in his Qatar media-week assessment. Separately, the FIA scheduled a closed International Court of Appeal hearing in Paris for 25 November on Audi's appeal of Italian GP Document 69. The public judgments index, checked on 27 November, did not list a decision for ICA-2026-14; Las Vegas Document 66 also notes the appeal.
items.why_it_matters: The titles are decided, but the nine-point P3 contest gives the Qatar race-week standings context. The appeal hearing notice does not itself change a race result or the points table; do not infer its outcome.

items.title: Haas confirms Bearman for 2027; Câmara set for Qatar
items.summary: TGR Haas confirmed on 26 November that Oliver Bearman has signed a new deal for 2027, completing next year's driver grid. Separately, Haas confirmed that Rafael Câmara will drive the final two 2026 Grands Prix and partner Bearman next season; Formula1.com reported that Freddie Slater will take Câmara's F2 seat for the final two rounds.
items.why_it_matters: The 2027 Haas line-up is settled, but this announcement does not change the Qatar 2026 entry list. Câmara's Qatar participation is confirmed; his F2 replacement does not establish any additional FP1 substitutions.

items.title: Verstappen/Russell tension and Ferrari clash follow F1 to Qatar
items.summary: Formula1.com's 25 November Qatar preview recounts the continuing Verstappen-Russell verbal dispute and Ferrari's Las Vegas fallout: Charles Leclerc hit team-mate Lewis Hamilton during their Turn 7 fight. FIA Document 60 found Leclerc wholly responsible and imposed a 10-second penalty; team principal Fred Vasseur described the incident as unacceptable. At Thursday's FIA press conference, Leclerc said Ferrari needed a solution, accepted responsibility for the Vegas clash, and declined to disclose whether the rules of engagement would change. He also denied having a contractual number-one clause. Neither statement establishes the team's operational race instructions. A 26 November media-day report quotes Hamilton saying securing second in the Constructors' Championship is Ferrari's immediate priority, the drivers remain free to race, and process/communication improvements will be discussed over winter. The Race's Qatar day-one report says Antonelli described a Mercedes software safety feature added after the Vegas battery-deployment loss; this is a reported team change, not a change to FIA limits or a validated Qatar outcome. Formula1.com's Russell/Verstappen update adds that Russell found some post-race comments "quite amusing", is moving on and does not want to continue the off-track exchange; Verstappen said there was nothing else to add and that his focus was Qatar.
items.why_it_matters: The Vegas penalty is final and does not become a Qatar ruling. Leclerc's contract denial and the drivers' comments do not establish team race instructions or a new rule. Attribute the Mercedes software update to The Race; do not treat it as an FIA energy-limit change or a confirmed on-track result. Keep Russell and Verstappen quotes attributed, not as predictions.
